label: D2 a1->S1 common: larger after unrewarded/a2 or rare trials, later in episode
terms: (phase == D2) * ~((action == 1) & (state == 1)) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) * (state == 1) * (prev_action == 2)
explanation: Fires only at D2 after choosing a1 and reaching S1 (common); zero at D1/GO and on other D2 transitions (negative term cancels the D2 timing baseline). Within a1->S1, magnitude grows with episode decile and is raised by an unrewarded previous trial (+0.55) and an unrewarded trial before that (+0.26), most by a previous a1 S2 u (rare-unrewarded, evidence for S1, +0.42 extra), and lowered when the previous trial was a1 S1 u (-0.74, roughly cancelling the no-reward boost) or an a2 choice (-0.54). So it is largest on the first a1->S1 after a non-reward that was not itself at S1, and decays over runs of rewarded a1->S1 trials (about 2.4 -> 1.9 -> 1.2 -> 0.5). The ideal-observer belief_lo adds nothing once trial history is in (weight ~0, dev 0.647 with vs 0.646 without), so it was dropped. All terms are observed (D2 choice and state are known). Test R^2 beyond timing 0.63 vs all-observed reference 0.52 and all ceiling 0.65; the model-policy decile alone gave 0.43, so dropping model outputs costs essentially nothing here.

issues: Most of the claims hold up. The original terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.634, matching the report. The feature is exactly 0 at D1 and GO, and D2 on non-a1->S1 trials is cancelled by a fitted weight of -0.171. Adding belief_lo gets weight -0.012 and leaves R^2 at 0.634, so it really adds nothing. tv('reward',-3) adds nothing either (0.634).

There is a large systematic error at the late-episode peaks. In the misses output, the worst-fit dev windows are all a1->S1 trials around t79-t93 that come right after a non-reward. Actual values are about 2.3-2.5 against predictions of 1.1-1.6, and the next rewarded a1->S1 trials (actual about 1.5-1.9) are predicted at 0.45-0.9. The model treats the episode effect as a separate additive slope (ep_dec weight +0.04), but in fact the history effects grow with episode time.

The no-reward boost depends heavily on episode decile. Split by decile, prev_reward==0 on a1->S1 gets weight +0.56 at ep_dec<3, +0.77 at 3-6 and +1.25 at >=7 (test 0.655). So the single '+0.55' in the explanation describes no particular part of the episode. Making the history terms scale with ep_dec raises test R^2 to 0.675-0.689, above the claimed additive ceiling of 0.65.

One history effect is missing. After an a1 S2 r trial (rare rewarded, which is evidence for S2), a1->S1 activation is lower: weight -0.42, and test R^2 goes from 0.634 to 0.644. Misses also shows 'D2 after a1 S2 r' as the most over-predicted cell (-0.172). The explanation lists a2 choices and a1 S1 u as the reducers but not this one.

Calling it 'explained' is not wrong, since test 0.634 against a ceiling of 0.65 is high. But the label says 'later in episode' as if that were a separate main effect. The data show the history dependence itself scales up over the episode, and the original terms miss about 0.055 of test R^2 because of that.
